committees_and_bodies.body: Constituent route: chair and ranking member district and state offices
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Not a committee. This entry answers the brief's recurring question of whether a chair's own office beats the committee. Rule of thumb, verified against the contact structures above: for almost every committee in this list, a constituent should go to the member's own district or state office first, and a non-constituent should go to the committee or to an organization that has standing with it.
committees_and_bodies.business: Not applicable.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Find your representative at https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative and your senators at https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm. Congressional offices systematically deprioritize mail from non-constituents; most Senate and House web forms require an in-state or in-district address and will reject others. Committee staff, by contrast, are policy staff who read substantive material regardless of its origin but have no casework obligation to anyone.
committees_and_bodies.note: Guidance entry, included because the per-committee 'chair's own office vs committee' question has a consistent answer. Specific cases where the committee beats the member's office: House and Senate Appropriations during the spring public-witness window (open to all, formal record); House Judiciary, House Oversight, House Financial Services, Senate HSGAC/PSI and Senate Intelligence whistleblower intakes (open to all, for factual allegations); and GAAIA@mail.house.gov for the Great American AI Act draft (open to all).

committees_and_bodies.body: Assembly Committee on Privacy and Consumer Protection
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Primary Assembly committee of first referral for AI, algorithmic decision-making, chatbot, data-privacy and AI-transparency bills (e.g. SB 53, AB 1064, AB 1018, companion-chatbot bills). Also runs a joint hearing track with the Select Committee on Biotechnology and Medical Technology on AI in health.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 53 (Transparency in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Act, Wiener) — signed 25 Sep 2025. 2026 follow-ons signed: SB 813 (independent verification organizations, signed 9 Sep 2026), AB 1405 (AI auditor registry, signed 9 Sep 2026), SB 1119 + SB 867 (companion chatbots / AI toys, signed 10 Sep 2026), AB 1709, AB 1856, AB 2246 (minors/design code, signed 10 Sep 2026), SB 1050 (synthetic performer disclosure, signed 16 Sep 2026). Pending on Governor's desk as of 22 Sep 2026: SB 1000, AB 2713, AB 1609, SB 1111, SB 947, AB 1883.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — SB 53 in force; CA Dept. of Technology begins annual threshold reviews in 2027. EO N-9-26 (18 Sep 2026) accelerates SB 813/AB 1405 implementation and directs work toward a frontier-model 'kill switch'. 2026 session closed; ~two dozen AI bills signed 9–16 Sep 2026.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — strongest and most underused route in the country. Any individual may register once and file a formal position letter (Support / Oppose / Amend) on any bill through the Legislature's Advocates portal; the letter is entered into the committee's official bill file and summarized in the committee analysis. Deadline convention for this committee: 12:00 noon on the Tuesday one week before the Tuesday hearing. Written testimony submitted this way is public comment and may be read into the record. In-person testimony at the hearing is open (two primary witnesses per side plus an open 'me-too' line); telephonic testimony has been discontinued.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: CA Attorney General (oag.ca.gov — AI legal advisories, Jan 2025; exclusive SB 53 civil enforcement); California Privacy Protection Agency for automated decision-making technology under the CCPA ADMT regs (https://cppa.ca.gov/regulations/ccpa_updates.html); California Civil Rights Department for FEHA automated-decision-system employment rules. Consumer complaints: https://oag.ca.gov/report
committees_and_bodies.note: The position-letter portal is open to 'individuals' as a registration category, not just lobbyists — confirmed on the portal itself. This is the single highest-leverage public-participation channel in US state AI policy and is dominated by trade associations.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Committee on Judiciary
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of first referral for frontier-AI safety, liability, digital replica, civil-rights and privacy AI bills. SB 53's Senate policy vehicle.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 53 (TFAIA, 2025); SB 813 (independent verification organizations, signed 9 Sep 2026); SB 1111 (digital replicas, pending); SB 947 (automated employment decisions, pending, would take effect 1 Jul 2027).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — Umberg appointed Judiciary chair for the 2025–2026 session; still chair at close of the 2026 session.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — position letters accepted from any member of the public via the Advocates portal, by email to sjud.fax@sen.ca.gov, by fax (916) 403-7394, or by mail (1021 O Street, Room 3240, Sacramento CA 95814). Deadline: 12:00 p.m. the Tuesday before the hearing unless otherwise stated. Committee staff explicitly warn they do not forward letters to individual members' offices, so copy members directly.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Same as Assembly entry — CA AG (oag.ca.gov/report), CPPA, California Civil Rights Department.
committees_and_bodies.note: Committee letter-policy page and deadline verified on sjud.senate.ca.gov 22 Sep 2026. Member roster not enumerated on the landing page; use the site's Members tab.

committees_and_bodies.body: Government Operations Agency / CPPA / Attorney General (executive AI oversight)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Implementation and enforcement of SB 53, SB 813 and AB 1405; ADMT regulation; FEHA automated-decision rules.
committees_and_bodies.business: Executive Order N-9-26 (18 Sep 2026) — directs GovOps, with Cal OES, to convene national experts and deliver recommendations within two months on onsite audits of frontier labs, independent verification of safety frameworks, an emergency shutoff mechanism, and an expanded definition of critical safety incidents to cover loss-of-control scenarios.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — EO issued 18 Sep 2026; recommendations due approximately Nov 2026.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Expert convening under EO N-9-26 is not a public hearing, but CPPA rulemaking is subject to full APA public comment, and the Joint California Policy Working Group on AI Frontier Models took public input. Watch cppa.ca.gov for comment windows.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: https://oag.ca.gov/report (AG consumer/civil-rights complaints); CPPA complaints via cppa.ca.gov; California Civil Rights Department for employment AI discrimination.
committees_and_bodies.note: Not a legislative committee — included because EO N-9-26 is the live implementation vehicle for California frontier-AI oversight and the comment windows are the practical participation route between sessions.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Standing Committee on Internet and Technology
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Lead Senate committee for AI, frontier-model safety, algorithmic pricing, AI training-data transparency and companion-chatbot bills. Held a dedicated public hearing on AI in consequential/high-risk contexts on 15 Jan 2026.
committees_and_bodies.business: RAISE Act, S6953B / A6453B (Gounardes / Bores) — signed 19 Dec 2025 (chapter amendments negotiated with Gov. Hochul). 2026 passed and awaiting Hochul action: A3411B (generative-AI inaccuracy notice, passed Senate 9 Mar 2026); A6578/S6955 (AI training-data transparency); A10379/S9051 (companion chatbots + 5-year AI children's-toy moratorium); A9349/S8623 (One Fair Price Act, surveillance pricing); A9581/S8706 (AI employment-impact reporting).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — RAISE Act takes effect 1 January 2027. Chapter amendments lowered the 'large developer' trigger from $100M compute spend to $500M annual revenue and cut penalties from $10–30M to $1–3M. 2026 bills remain on the Governor's desk; she has until year-end 2026 to act.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL but real. Two routes: (1) any New Yorker can register a formal position on any bill directly on its NYSenate.gov page using the 'Aye'/'Nay' buttons with a written comment — the position and comment are transmitted immediately to that person's own senator's office; this is free, open, and almost entirely unused by the public. (2) For a noticed committee public hearing, testimony is by hearing-specific reply form circulated with the hearing notice, filed in advance with the committee; written statements are accepted from anyone even without speaking.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: New York Attorney General — exclusive RAISE Act civil enforcement (complaints: https://ag.ny.gov/complaint-forms). Separate frontier-AI oversight office created inside the Department of Financial Services to assess large frontier developers, collect fees, issue regulations and publish annual reports (https://www.dfs.ny.gov).
committees_and_bodies.note: Ranking minority member: Daniel G. Stec (R/C/IP, SD-45), verified 2026-09-22. Members: Gounardes, Hinchey, Parker, Walczyk, Zellner.

committees_and_bodies.body: Assembly Standing Committee on Science and Technology
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Assembly committee of reference for AI, emerging-technology and frontier-model bills. Alex Bores, the RAISE Act Assembly sponsor, sits on it.
committees_and_bodies.business: A6453B (RAISE Act, Bores) — signed 19 Dec 2025, effective 1 Jan 2027; A6578 (AI training-data transparency); A10379 (companion chatbots); A9349 (One Fair Price Act); A9581 (AI employment-impact reporting); A3411B (generative-AI notice).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — members listed 22 Sep 2026: Blumencranz, Bores, Burke, Conrad, Durso, Gibbs, Hooks, Vanel.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL — the Assembly does not run a general online bill-comment tool equivalent to the Senate's. Participation is via (a) written testimony to noticed Assembly or joint public hearings, submitted to the committee in advance per the hearing notice, and (b) direct written submissions to the chair and your own member. Anyone may submit written testimony to a public hearing without appearing.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: NY Attorney General (https://ag.ny.gov/complaint-forms); NY Department of Financial Services frontier-AI oversight office.
committees_and_bodies.note: Ranking minority member not published on the committee page; Blumencranz and Durso are the Republican members listed.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Committee on Business, Labor, & Technology
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of reference for AI, automated decision-making technology, consumer protection and technology bills. SB 26-189 was referred here.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 26-189 'Automated Decision-Making Technology' (Rodriguez, Coleman / Duran, Bacon) — repeals and replaces the Colorado AI Act (SB 24-205). Signed 14 May 2026, effective 1 Jan 2027. Predecessor history: SB 24-205 enacted 2024; SB 25B-004 (Aug 2025 special session) pushed its effective date to 30 Jun 2026; AG delayed enforcement Apr 2026; a federal court then restrained enforcement.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED, WITH LITIGATION RISK — SB 26-189 drops SB 24-205's algorithmic-discrimination duty of care and risk-management program in favor of disclosure/transparency plus consumer rights over ADMT in consequential decisions. A federal district court ordered the AG not to initiate enforcement of SB 24-205 or replacement legislation for conduct occurring before 14 days after it rules on x.AI's preliminary-injunction motion, so the 1 Jan 2027 date is not secure.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — Colorado is one of the most open states. Any member of the public may testify in person OR remotely by video at a committee hearing, and may submit written testimony, after registering through the General Assembly's Public Testimony Registration system. Register in advance of the hearing (sign-ups typically open once the hearing is noticed and close shortly before it starts). Written testimony is accepted from anyone and is distributed to committee members.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Colorado Attorney General — exclusive enforcement under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act; ADMT violations are deceptive trade practices. Complaints: https://coag.gov/file-complaint/
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Nick Hinrichsen. Members: Marc Catlin, Iman Jodeh, Larry Liston. See also https://content.leg.colorado.gov/agencies/senate/participation-legislative-hearings for the hearing-participation rules.

committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: House committee of reference for AI, ADMT, technology and labor bills; the House-side counterpart that heard the AI replacement legislation.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 26-189 (Automated Decision-Making Technology), House sponsors Reps. Monica Duran and Jennifer Bacon. Signed 14 May 2026, effective 1 Jan 2027.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — same litigation caveat as the Senate entry (x.AI challenge).

committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Colorado Attorney General, Consumer Protection Section — https://coag.gov/file-complaint/
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Sean Camacho. House guide: https://content.leg.colorado.gov/agencies/house-representatives/guide-public-hearings

committees_and_bodies.body: House Committee on Delivery of Government Efficiency
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: House committee that heard and reported TRAIGA (HB 149) in the 89th Legislature; jurisdiction over state technology, AI governance and government efficiency.
committees_and_bodies.business: HB 149, Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA), Capriglione — passed House 147-0, Senate 31-0; signed June 2025; IN FORCE since 1 January 2026. Companion 89R AI bills: SB 1964 (state-agency AI use), HB 2818 (AI Division inside DIR), SB 441 and HB 3133 (deepfakes), SB 2420 (App Store Accountability), SB 1188 (health records/AI), HB 3512 (state-employee AI training).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED, IN FORCE — TRAIGA is intent-based, bars a private right of action, preempts local AI ordinances, gives the AG a 60-day cure period, creates a 7-member Texas Artificial Intelligence Council inside DIR and a 36-month AI regulatory sandbox administered by DIR.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES, and unusually easy. Texas runs a dedicated online House Public Comment portal: any member of the public can submit a written comment for or against any bill set for a House committee hearing, from anywhere, without travelling to Austin. Comments are accepted from the time the hearing is posted until the committee closes the record (typically shortly after the hearing adjourns). In-person witness registration is done at Capitol kiosks or via the committee clerk. Note: 2026 is an interim year — the 90th Legislature convenes January 2027 — so the live route right now is interim-charge hearings.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Texas Attorney General — sole TRAIGA enforcement authority; TRAIGA required the AG to stand up an online AI complaint mechanism. AI rights and complaint route: https://www.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumer-protection/file-consumer-complaint/consumer-ai-rights ; portal: https://consumerprotection.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumercomplaintportal/s/ . Civil penalties $10,000–$200,000.
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Salman Bhojani. Also relevant: Texas Artificial Intelligence Council (7 public members, within DIR) created by TRAIGA.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Committee on Business and Commerce
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of referral for TRAIGA (HB 149) and holder of the 2026 interim charge to evaluate 'the regulation and use of artificial intelligence systems' under SB 1964 and HB 149, plus data-center growth and grid impacts.
committees_and_bodies.business: HB 149 (TRAIGA) — Senate sponsor route; SB 1964 (state agency AI). 2026 interim charges from Lt. Gov. Patrick direct this committee to review AI regulation and data centers ahead of the 90th Legislature (Jan 2027).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — TRAIGA in force since 1 Jan 2026; interim review under way through 2026 (committee took up AI and jobs in a hearing week of 21 Sep 2026).
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — the Texas Senate takes public testimony at interim and session hearings. Unlike the House there is no general online comment portal for Senate committees: register to testify with the committee clerk (Annika Vandayar, (512) 463-0365, Sam Houston Building Room 370) and submit written testimony to the clerk in advance, per the notice posted on Texas Legislature Online. Interim hearings are the most accessible moment because the record is open and the committee is actively taking input for 2027 bills.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Texas Attorney General AI complaint portal — https://consumerprotection.texasattorneygeneral.gov/consumercomplaintportal/s/ ; Texas AI Council and AI sandbox at the Department of Information Resources (dir.texas.gov).
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Phil King. Other 2026 interim AI charges sit with House State Affairs (data centers), House Public Health, House Public Education, House Judiciary & Civil Jurisprudence, and Senate Economic Development (AI workforce impact).

committees_and_bodies.body: House Committee on Cybersecurity, Data Analytics, & IT (with its Artificial Intelligence Subcommittee, HCDA-HAIE)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Primary House committee for AI, data privacy, algorithmic systems and social-media bills. Has three standing subcommittees: Artificial Intelligence (HAIE), Data Privacy and Analytics (HDPA), and Social Media and Content Moderation (HSMC).
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 315, Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act — Senate sponsor Sen. Mary Edly-Allen (D-Grayslake), House sponsor Rep. Daniel Didech (D-Buffalo Grove). Passed Senate 52-5 and House 110-0; signed by Gov. Pritzker 6 July 2026; effective 1 January 2027 (some analyses cite full compliance obligations phasing to 2028). Also in force: HB 3773 (AI in employment decisions under the Illinois Human Rights Act, effective 1 Jan 2026); the AI Video Interview Act; and the WOPR Act restricting AI therapy.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED for the legislation; UNVERIFIED for the chair. SB 315 is the first US state law to require independent third-party safety audits of frontier developers (models from developers with >$500M annual revenue), publication of safety frameworks, catastrophic-risk reporting, and 72-hour (24-hour for imminent risk) incident reporting. Enforced by the Illinois Attorney General with penalties up to $1M first violation / $3M subsequent.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — Illinois has the single most frictionless public-position system of any state: the electronic WITNESS SLIP. Any person may file a slip on any bill before any committee hearing, recording their name, whether they represent themselves or an organization, and their position (Proponent / Opponent / No Position), with an option to request to testify orally or submit a record of appearance only. No lobbyist registration, no fee. Slips are counted and displayed publicly and legislators visibly react to the tallies. Deadline convention: file at least one hour before the hearing (ideally the day before); the Senate accepts and allows edits until the end of the hearing day, the House until the hearing concludes. A separate slip is required for each committee hearing and for each amendment.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Illinois Attorney General — enforcement of the AI Safety Measures Act; consumer fraud complaints at https://www.illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/file-a-complaint/consumer/ . For AI employment discrimination under HB 3773: Illinois Department of Human Rights (dhr.illinois.gov).
committees_and_bodies.note: CHAIR UNVERIFIED — the ILGA site blocked automated retrieval of the committee detail page and no 2025–2026 source names the chair. Prior chairs (Jaime Andrade 2017, Lamont Robinson 2023) have both left the role. Verify by phone with the House Clerk or at ilga.gov/House/Committees. Committee composition for 2025–2026 is 8 Democrats / 4 Republicans. Witness slips are filed from the specific hearing page, e.g. https://ilga.gov/House/hearings — the linked PDF is the official ILGA tutorial.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Executive Committee (with its AI and Social Media Subcommittee, SEXC-AISM)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of reference for the 2026 AI package; the AI and Social Media subcommittee sits under Executive. SB 315 and the companion Senate AI bills were heard on this track in May 2026.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 315 (AI Safety Measures Act, Edly-Allen) — signed 6 Jul 2026, effective 1 Jan 2027. Companion 2026 Senate package: SB 316 (chatbot safeguards, Ellman), SB 317 (customer-service chatbot disclosure, Ventura), SB 318 (ticket-resale bots, Stadelman), SB 340 (consumer data, Murphy), SB 343 (rental pricing algorithms, Guzmán), SB 415 (facial recognition in schools, Villa), SB 416 (AI classroom grading, Martwick).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — package reported out of committee 13 May 2026; SB 315 signed. Illinois is the only state so far to add mandatory third-party frontier-model audits on top of the California/New York disclosure model.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — electronic witness slips, same system as the House. Senate slips may be submitted and edited until the end of the hearing day. Anyone may file as an individual; you do not need to attend or speak.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul — AI Safety Measures Act enforcement; consumer complaints https://www.illinoisattorneygeneral.gov/file-a-complaint/consumer/
committees_and_bodies.note: Executive Committee chair verified via the Illinois Senate Democrats' official 104th GA committee-assignment page, 2026-09-22. The AI and Social Media subcommittee is listed on ILGA as SEXC-AISM but had no scheduled hearings at time of check; its chair is not separately published.

committees_and_bodies.body: House Technology, Economic Development & Veterans Committee (TEDV)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Explicitly holds artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, broadband and telecommunications jurisdiction. All three major 2026 AI bills were heard here on 15 Jan 2026.
committees_and_bodies.business: HB 2225 (AI companion chatbots, prime sponsor Rep. Lisa Callan, by request of Gov. Ferguson) — House 69-28, Senate 43-5, concurrence 74-21, SIGNED 24 March 2026 as Chapter 168, Laws of 2026, effective 1 January 2027; companion SB 5984. Also 2026: HB 1170 (deepfake detection/disclosure for providers with >1M users, E2SHB reported to Senate Ways & Means Feb 2026); HB 2157 (high-risk AI discrimination, Rep. Cindy Ryu).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — HB 2225 enacted (C 168 L 26). HB 1170 and HB 2157 did not reach enactment in 2026; expect reintroduction in the 2027 session.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — Washington's Committee Sign-In (CSI) system is the best-designed remote testimony portal in the country and is wide open. For any scheduled hearing, any member of the public can (a) sign in PRO / CON / OTHER on a bill in under a minute with no account and no travel — these positions are tallied and reported to the committee; (b) submit written testimony that becomes part of the legislative record; or (c) register to testify remotely by video or in person. Deadline convention: written testimony and position sign-in generally close one hour before the hearing; remote-testimony registration typically closes 24 hours before. Meetings are hybrid by default.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Washington Attorney General — Consumer Protection Division (https://www.atg.wa.gov/file-complaint); the AG's Office also hosts the statutory Washington State AI Task Force.
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Shelley Kloba (D-1). Ranking Minority Member: Stephanie Barnard (R-8). Composition 10 D / 3 R. How-to-testify guide: https://leg.wa.gov/bills-meetings-and-session/session/how-to-testify-at-a-committee-meeting/

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Environment, Energy & Technology Committee (ENET)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of referral for AI and telecommunications bills, including HB 2225 on its Senate passage.
committees_and_bodies.business: HB 2225 / SB 5984 (AI companion chatbots) — signed 24 Mar 2026, C 168 L 26, effective 1 Jan 2027. E2SHB 1170 (deepfakes) received a Senate bill report Feb 2026.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — HB 2225 enacted; HB 1170 stalled at Senate Ways & Means.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — same CSI portal, Senate instance. Sign in PRO/CON/OTHER, upload written testimony, or register for remote video testimony. Positions are counted even if you never speak, which makes this the cheapest meaningful civic action available on a state AI bill.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Washington Attorney General Consumer Protection (https://www.atg.wa.gov/file-complaint); Washington State AI Task Force at https://www.atg.wa.gov/aitaskforce
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chairs: Victoria Hunt and Vandana Slatter. Ranking Minority Member: Matt Boehnke (R). Composition 7 D / 4 R; members include Dhingra, Harris, Liias, Lovelett, MacEwen, Short, Wellman.

committees_and_bodies.body: Washington State Artificial Intelligence Task Force (Office of the Attorney General)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Statutory 19-member task force created by ESSB 5838 (2024), housed in the AG's Office, assessing AI use across sectors and recommending legislation.
committees_and_bodies.business: ESSB 5838 (2024). Final Report issued July 2026, containing 11 policy recommendations plus three commissioned research studies on AI risks, worker sentiment, and existing regulation.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — final report published July 2026; the task force fed directly into the 2026 bills (HB 2225, HB 1170, HB 2157).
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL — task force meetings are public, recorded and carried on TVW, and minutes are published on the AG's site, but a formal public-comment procedure is not published. Contact the AG's Office directly to submit input. The legislative CSI portal remains the reliable public route.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Washington Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division — https://www.atg.wa.gov/file-complaint
committees_and_bodies.note: Membership spans legislators, academia, labor, industry and community advocates. No single named chair is published on the task force landing page.

committees_and_bodies.body: Joint Committee on General Law — Senate co-chair
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Connecticut's lead committee on AI, consumer protection and data privacy. Sen. Maroney has driven CT's AI agenda from this chair since 2023.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 5, the Connecticut Artificial Intelligence Responsibility and Transparency Act (CART Act) — PUBLIC ACT 26-15, signed by Gov. Lamont 2 June 2026. Covers employment AI disclosure, frontier-developer obligations, AI companion/chatbot safeguards including suicidal-ideation detection, youth online safety, an AI Academy and AI literacy training, and an AI regulatory sandbox. Predecessor: SB 2 (2024, 2025) which passed the Senate but did not become law.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — PA 26-15 enacted. Staggered effective dates: 1 Oct 2026 (employment AI framework and frontier-developer provisions), 1 Jan 2027 (AI companion regulations), 1 Oct 2027 (main employment disclosure requirements).
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — Connecticut is one of the most genuinely open testimony regimes in the US. For every public hearing, any member of the public may submit written testimony through the committee's online submission form and/or sign up to speak. There is no residency, registration or organizational requirement. Deadline convention: written testimony must be submitted before the start of the hearing (committees typically post a cut-off of 24 hours prior for guaranteed distribution); speaker sign-up for major hearings is by lottery opening roughly 24 hours before. All testimony — written and spoken — is permanent public record, posted on the CGA website and indexed by search engines, including your name, address, phone and email.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Connecticut Attorney General — exclusive enforcement over the CART Act's employment-AI provisions (https://portal.ct.gov/ag). Connecticut Department of Consumer Protection for consumer-facing matters.
committees_and_bodies.note: Senate ranking member: Paul Cicarella (R-34). Senate vice chair: John W. Fonfara (D-1). Connecticut uses joint House/Senate committees, so this committee is one body with two co-chairs; listed twice here to capture both chambers' leadership. Participation guide: https://www.cga.ct.gov/asp/content/yourvoice.asp

committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — Massachusetts accepts online written testimony from any member of the public for any noticed hearing. Sign-up to speak is handled per hearing notice. Deadline convention: testimony is generally accepted up to and for a short window after the hearing, but committees ask for submission by the hearing start.

committees_and_bodies.body: Joint Committee on Economic Development and Emerging Technologies — Senate chair
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: The committee that actually produced Massachusetts' frontier-AI safety language, attached to the economic development bond bill.
committees_and_bodies.business: H.5527, An Act relative to Massachusetts winning global investment, talent, and innovation ('Mass Wins Act') — released by this committee 22 June 2026 with frontier-AI provisions covering labs with >$500M annual AI-derived revenue or >$1B annual AI R&D: catastrophic-capability identification, mitigation, third-party review by independent evaluators at least every six months, whistleblower protections, critical-safety-incident reporting, and AG enforcement by court order. Anthropic publicly backed the provisions.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — NOT ENACTED as of 22 Sep 2026. H.5527 was superseded by a new draft (H.5562) on 8 July 2026; the Senate passed its version (S.3178) on 24 July 2026 with responsible-AI provisions. The bill is in CONFERENCE COMMITTEE. On 18 Sep 2026 Gov. Healey publicly pressed the conferees to strengthen it with independent reviews of the most powerful models and faster serious-incident reporting.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — online written testimony via MyLegislature for any noticed hearing of this committee. NOTE: the bill is now in conference, where there are no public hearings; the effective route at this stage is written comment directly to the six conferees and to the Governor's office, plus testimony when the next session's bills are heard.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Massachusetts Attorney General (Chapter 93A AI advisory) — https://www.mass.gov/how-to/file-a-consumer-complaint ; Massachusetts AI Hub (created by the 2024 Mass Leads Act, $100M).
committees_and_bodies.note: Senate vice chair: Nick Collins. Senate ranking minority: Peter J. Durant. THIS IS THE LIVE MASSACHUSETTS AI FIGHT as of late September 2026 and the conference committee is the pressure point.

committees_and_bodies.body: Joint Committee on Economic Development and Emerging Technologies — House chair
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: House-side leadership on the frontier-AI provisions of the economic development bill.
committees_and_bodies.business: H.5527 → H.5562 / S.3178 ('Mass Wins Act') frontier-AI safety provisions; in conference committee as of 22 Sep 2026.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — unresolved; Gov. Healey is pushing publicly for stronger independent-evaluation and incident-reporting language.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES for committee hearings via MyLegislature online testimony; no hearings during conference.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Massachusetts Attorney General — https://www.mass.gov/how-to/file-a-consumer-complaint
committees_and_bodies.note: House vice chair: Jessica Ann Giannino. House ranking minority: Michael J. Soter.

committees_and_bodies.body: House Committee on Communications, Technology and Innovation
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Primary House committee for AI, technology and innovation bills, with a Technology and Innovation Subcommittee. 28 members (20 D / 8 R); meets 10:00 a.m. Mondays, House Committee Room C-206.
committees_and_bodies.business: HB 2094, High-Risk Artificial Intelligence Developer and Deployer Act (2025) — passed both chambers 20 Feb 2025, VETOED by Gov. Youngkin March 2025; would have taken effect 1 July 2026 with exclusive AG enforcement. 2026 session: most AI bills CONTINUED TO 2027 — HB 668 (AI therapy), HB 1294 (police AI disclosure), HB 310 (AI workforce reports), HB 982 (campaign-ad AI disclosure), HB 825 (ticket-resale bots), SB 586 (health-carrier AI claims disclosure, Salim), and Del. Maldonado's children's-chatbot bill. Still advancing in 2026: SB 394 / HB 1186 (Pekarsky/Rasoul) requiring state guidance on AI in schools.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — Virginia has NO comprehensive AI statute. The 2026 session under Gov. Spanberger largely deferred AI legislation to 2027, with legislators citing the December 2025 federal executive order and its child-safety carve-out. Executive action instead: EXECUTIVE ORDER 22, signed 18 September 2026, creating Virginia's first AI task force (data privacy, cybersecurity, workforce displacement) alongside data-center accountability measures.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES, and Virginia is unusually low-friction: citizens DO NOT need to register in advance to speak in person at a committee or subcommittee meeting — the chair invites members of the audience to speak. For remote participation the House runs HODSpeak, an online portal through which any member of the public can sign up to give remote testimony on a bill before a House committee. Note Senate subcommittees do not offer remote testimony. Session is short (roughly Jan–Mar), so the window is narrow; the 2027 session is where the continued AI bills return.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Virginia Attorney General — would have held exclusive enforcement under HB 2094; currently handles AI matters under the Virginia Consumer Protection Act (https://www.oag.state.va.us/consumer-protection/index.php/file-a-complaint). Also the new EO 22 AI task force.
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Irene Shin (D-8). Clerk: Robert Asplund, (804) 698-1946. General participation guidance: https://vga.virginia.gov/engage/participation-public-comment/

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Committee on General Laws and Technology
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of reference for AI, technology, data and general-laws bills. Meets in Senate Room B (Room 306), 30 minutes after adjournment on Wednesdays.
committees_and_bodies.business: HB 2094 (2025, vetoed). 2026: SB 586 (Salim, health-carrier AI disclosure) continued to 2027; SB 796 (children's chatbot restrictions); SB 394 (Pekarsky, AI guidance for schools) advancing.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — no comprehensive Virginia AI law; most 2026 AI bills carried over to the 2027 session.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — no advance registration is required to speak in person at Senate committee meetings; the chair may invite audience members to testify. Remote public testimony for Senate STANDING committees is available through the Senate's committee-meetings page; Senate SUBCOMMITTEES do not offer remote testimony. Written statements may be filed with the committee clerk (Eric Bingham).
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Virginia Attorney General consumer complaint — https://www.oag.state.va.us/consumer-protection/index.php/file-a-complaint ; Governor's AI task force under Executive Order 22 (18 Sep 2026).
committees_and_bodies.note: Chair and roster verified from the official 2026 Senate Committee Chart (https://apps.senate.virginia.gov/Portal/Resources/Comcal.pdf). Members listed: Head, French, Locke, Jordan, Craig, Reeves, VanValkenburg, Williams Graves, Pillion, Roem, Marsden, Rouse, Carroll Foy, Pekarsky.

committees_and_bodies.body: House Business, Labor, and Commerce Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: House standing committee for AI consumer-protection, generative-AI disclosure and technology-commerce bills, including amendments to the Artificial Intelligence Policy Act and the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy.
committees_and_bodies.business: Utah Artificial Intelligence Policy Act (SB 149, 2024), narrowed by SB 226 (2025) which limited generative-AI disclosure duties to high-risk interactions and regulated occupations. 2026 session sent NINE AI bills to the Governor: HB 276 (nonconsensual deepfake intimate imagery, AI provenance disclosures, platform safeguards — Defay/Cullimore); SB 256 (defamation law extended to AI-generated content, unauthorized use of personal identity — Cullimore/Teuscher); HB 289 (AI-generated CSAM); SB 319 (human judgment required in insurance preauthorization, AI disclosure); SB 150 (restricts AI giving medical advice absent a practitioner-patient relationship); HB 273 and HB 218 (AI in schools and required digital-skills curriculum); SB 73 (age verification); SB 69 (school device restrictions). HB 320 (Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy Amendments) also moved in 2026.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — Utah's model is disclosure-plus-sandbox rather than risk-tiering. The Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy runs an AI Learning Laboratory offering regulatory mitigation agreements to participants.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL / CHAIR'S DISCRETION — Utah committee meetings are streamed live and also offered as a virtual meeting with an explicit 'option to provide public comment (at committee chair's discretion)'; to use it you join the virtual meeting and submit your name and email. In-person public comment at the hearing is also at the chair's discretion and time-limited. Utah's session is very short (45 days, Jan–Mar), so contacting the committee analyst (Rohnin Randles) ahead of the bill's hearing is the practical route.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Utah Division of Consumer Protection, which houses the Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy — enforcement of the AI Policy Act and administration of the AI Learning Laboratory. Complaints: https://dcp.utah.gov/complaints/
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Jason B. Kyle. 15 members (12 R / 3 D). Utah's Rep. Doug Fiefia (R) co-chairs the Future Caucus National Task Force on State AI Policy.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Business and Labor Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate standing committee for AI consumer-protection and technology-commerce bills, including SB 226 and the 2026 AI package.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 226 (2025, narrowing the AI Policy Act); 2026: SB 256 (AI defamation and identity), SB 319 (insurance preauthorization human review), SB 150 (AI medical advice — Vickers' own bill), SB 73 (age verification), SB 69 (school devices).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — nine AI bills cleared the 2026 general session; Utah continues to narrow broad disclosure duties while expanding targeted harms coverage (deepfakes, CSAM, health, insurance).
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL — same Utah convention: virtual meeting attendance with an option to provide public comment at the chair's discretion, plus in-person comment at the chair's discretion. Contact committee secretary Zoe Adams or analyst Rohnin Randles in advance of the hearing.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Utah Division of Consumer Protection / Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy — https://dcp.utah.gov/complaints/
committees_and_bodies.note: Members: Cullimore, Ipson, McCay, Musselman, Pitcher (D), Sandall, Weiler. Eight members total.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Education, Energy, and the Environment Committee (EEE)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of reference for AI in education, state AI governance and technology policy bills.
committees_and_bodies.business: SB 720, Artificial Intelligence Ready Schools Act (Hester, Attar, Brooks, Feldman and others; crossfile HB 1057) — Senate 41-0, House 129-8, APPROVED BY GOVERNOR 26 May 2026 as CHAPTER 634. Also 2026: SB 597, Maryland Artificial Intelligence Partnership Act (Chapter 633) creating the Maryland AI Partnership in the University System of Maryland, an AI Public Services Fellowship and an AI Incubation Lab; SB 114 (Chapter 434) 3-1-1 systems with AI. Foundation: Artificial Intelligence Governance Act of 2024 (SB 818, Chapter 496) — state AI inventory, Governor's AI Subcabinet, DoIT guardrails.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — Maryland's approach is government-capacity and education focused rather than private-sector risk regulation. A 2026 surveillance-pricing bill targeting AI-driven individualized pricing also moved.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — Maryland runs one of the most structured online witness systems. Create a free MyMGA account, log in, choose 'Witness Signup', find your bill, state your position (Favorable / Unfavorable / Favorable with Amendments), indicate whether you will testify orally or written-only, and upload your testimony as a PDF. HARD DEADLINE: the signup window is open only between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. TWO BUSINESS DAYS BEFORE the scheduled hearing. Miss it and you cannot file. Each committee publishes its own witness guidelines.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Maryland Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division (https://www.marylandattorneygeneral.gov/Pages/CPD/default.aspx); Maryland Department of Information Technology and the Governor's AI Subcabinet for state-agency AI; ai.maryland.gov for the state AI program.
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Cheryl C. Kagan. Chair verified through 2026 session committee testimony documents addressed to 'Chair Brian J. Feldman'. The two-business-day 8am–6pm witness window is the most commonly missed deadline in state AI advocacy.

committees_and_bodies.body: House Economic Matters Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: House committee of reference for AI consumer-protection, surveillance-pricing, business-regulation and technology-commerce bills. 19 members appointed by the Speaker.
committees_and_bodies.business: 2026 surveillance-pricing legislation restricting AI-driven individualized pricing; HB 1057 (crossfile of SB 720, AI Ready Schools, Chapter 634). Related: AI Governance Act of 2024 (SB 818).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — Maryland enacted targeted 2026 AI measures (education, state AI partnership, surveillance pricing) but no comprehensive private-sector AI risk statute.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — same MyMGA Witness Signup system. Submission window 8:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. two business days before the hearing. Economic Matters publishes its own witness guidelines PDF with panel rules and time limits.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Maryland Attorney General Consumer Protection Division; Maryland DoIT. Program hub: https://ai.maryland.gov/ai-maryland/legislation
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Lorig Charkoudian. Committee email aa_ecm@mga.maryland.gov, phone (410) 841-3519, House Office Building Room 231.

committees_and_bodies.body: Assembly Science, Innovation and Technology Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: The dedicated Assembly committee for AI, deepfakes, chatbots and emerging-technology bills. Released a five-bill AI transparency package on 17 March 2026.
committees_and_bodies.business: March 2026 AI package cleared by this committee: A4728, A4729, A4730, A4731, A4732 — AI transparency across chatbots, real-estate advertising, election information, professional licensing and commercial communications. Additional 2026-2027 bills: A5088, A5316, A4981, A3307, A2616. New Jersey's enacted AI law remains the deepfake statute; there is no comprehensive NJ AI act.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — package advanced out of committee 17 Mar 2026; no comprehensive NJ AI statute enacted as of 22 Sep 2026. New Jersey's most consequential AI rule is administrative, not legislative: see agency route.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — the NJ Legislature runs an online Committee Registrations system where members of the public register to testify at committee meetings; written statements may also be submitted to the committee aide in advance. Deadlines are set per meeting notice, usually the business day before. NJ agendas are often posted with little notice, so monitoring the committee schedule page is essential.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: STRONGEST NJ ROUTE — New Jersey Division on Civil Rights (Office of the Attorney General). AG Platkin and DCR issued Guidance on Algorithmic Discrimination (8 Jan 2025) holding that the NJ Law Against Discrimination applies to algorithmic and AI-driven discrimination in employment, housing, lending and places of public accommodation, and created a Civil Rights Innovation Lab. NJ adopted disparate-impact rules under the LAD in December 2025 with specific AI guidance. File a complaint: https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-on-civil-rights-home/
committees_and_bodies.note: Chair verified from the 17 Mar 2026 committee action reported contemporaneously. Tully also serves as vice-chair of Commerce, Economic Development and Agriculture. The NJ DCR complaint route is live NOW and does not require any new statute — an underused channel for AI hiring and housing discrimination.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Commerce Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of referral for AI consumer-protection and companion-chatbot bills.
committees_and_bodies.business: S4474, 'Establishes safety requirements for artificial intelligence companion operators' (Sens. Paul Moriarty and Angela McKnight, D) — introduced 18 June 2026, referred to Senate Commerce, PENDING IN COMMITTEE as of 22 Sep 2026. Also S1840, S2862. Senate Democrats separately moved legislation on energy demand from AI data centers.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED for the bill; CHAIR UNVERIFIED. S4474 has not advanced out of committee.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: YES — register through the Legislature's Committee Registrations portal to testify at a Senate committee meeting; written statements accepted via the committee aide. Because S4474 is stalled in committee, requesting a hearing from the chair and the sponsors is the operative action.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: NJ Division on Civil Rights algorithmic discrimination guidance and complaint route — https://www.njoag.gov/about/divisions-and-offices/division-on-civil-rights-home/ ; NJ Division of Consumer Affairs for consumer AI matters.
committees_and_bodies.note: CHAIR UNVERIFIED — the njleg.state.nj.us committee member pages did not render retrievable rosters for the 2026-2027 (222nd) Legislature. Verify with the Office of Legislative Services, 800-792-8630 or leginfo@njleg.org.

committees_and_bodies.body: House Commerce Finance and Policy Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: House committee of reference for AI chatbot, data-privacy, deepfake/'nudification' and consumer-protection bills. Meets Tue/Wed/Thu 8:15 a.m., Capitol 120.

chair.name: Tim O'Driscoll (R) and Erin Koegel (DFL) — CO-CHAIRS

committees_and_bodies.business: HF 4452, AI chatbot technology requirements with a private cause of action for harm (2026). HF 4456 and related 2026 AI and data-privacy bills. Minnesota's flagship enacted law is its AI 'nudification' ban — the nation's first — which xAI sued to block in July 2026; a federal judge DENIED xAI's request to pause the law, so the ban is in effect during the litigation. Penalties reach $500,000.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — nudification ban in force and surviving preliminary challenge; 2026 chatbot and AI bills advanced through committee. Minnesota also considered legislation denying free-speech rights to AI agents.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL — Minnesota has NO central online testimony portal. The rule is: 'members of the general public are encouraged to testify before committees, though testimony will need to be arranged with committee staff prior to a scheduled hearing.' Contact the committee administrator a day or two before the hearing; same-day sign-up is sometimes possible if time permits. Bring written copies to hand out. Committee administrators for this committee: Ben Frese (GOP) and Sam O'Neill (DFL). House Public Information Services: 651-296-2146.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Minnesota Attorney General — consumer protection and enforcement of the nudification statute; complaint form at https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Complaint.asp
committees_and_bodies.note: The 94th Legislature's House operated under a power-sharing arrangement, hence dual co-chairs. Vice chairs: Steve Elkins (DFL) and Bernie Perryman (R). Minnesota's arrange-with-staff convention makes it the least automated of the 13 states and therefore the one where a single phone call has the most disproportionate effect.

committees_and_bodies.body: Senate Commerce and Consumer Protection Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Senate committee of reference for AI consumer-facing bills, chatbot restrictions and data privacy. Meets Tue/Thu 12:30–2:30 p.m., Room G-15 Capitol.
committees_and_bodies.business: 2026 bipartisan Senate package on consumer-facing AI, including a proposed ban on minors' access to companion chatbots; SF 1886; companion measures to HF 4452. Minnesota's enacted AI nudification ban is the subject of xAI v. Minnesota (D. Minn., filed July 2026; preliminary injunction denied).
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — bipartisan Senate AI package presented and moving through committee in 2026; nudification ban in effect pending litigation.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL — arrange with committee staff in advance. Committee administrator: Bill Lunzer, 651-296-2090. Senate Information: 651-296-0504 or senate.information@senate.mn. No online portal; written testimony is delivered to the administrator for distribution to members.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: Minnesota Attorney General — https://www.ag.state.mn.us/Office/Complaint.asp
committees_and_bodies.note: Vice Chair: Judy Seeberger (DFL-41). Ranking Minority Member: Gary H. Dahms (R-15). Eleven members total.

committees_and_bodies.body: Future Caucus National Task Force on State AI Policy
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Cross-partisan task force of Gen Z and millennial state legislators developing shared AI governance approaches across states; hosts public hearings and confidential briefings and produces a Bipartisan State AI Policy Memo.

chair.name: Rep. Monique Priestley (D-Vermont) and Rep. Doug Fiefia (R-Utah) — CO-CHAIRS

committees_and_bodies.business: Not a legislating body. Priestley authored Vermont's AI legislation; Fiefia authored Utah's social-media data-control law. The task force advises on model language that recurs across state bills.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — launched July 2025, active through 2026; the most useful cross-state map of where AI language originates before it appears in individual state bills.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: PARTIAL — the task force states it will 'host public hearings'; these are the practical entry point for members of the public who want to reach multiple state legislators at once. Legislator membership is by application (Gen Z and millennial state lawmakers). The public engages through the organization's contact channels and public hearing announcements.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: N/A — advocacy and convening body, not an enforcement agency.
committees_and_bodies.note: Included per the AI caucus/task force request. Other state-level bodies worth tracking: Washington State AI Task Force (AG's office, final report July 2026); Virginia's AI task force under Executive Order 22 (18 Sep 2026); Maryland's Governor's AI Subcabinet (SB 818, 2024); the Texas Artificial Intelligence Council (7 public members, inside DIR, created by TRAIGA); Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy and AI Learning Laboratory; and New York's frontier-AI oversight office inside the Department of Financial Services.

committees_and_bodies.body: White House AI Litigation Task Force / Department of Commerce BEAD conditions
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Not a state committee — included because it materially changes the status of every state AI law listed above and is the reason several 2026 state bills were tabled.
committees_and_bodies.business: December 2025 Executive Order establishing an AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws deemed not 'minimally burdensome', and directing Commerce to explore withholding BEAD broadband funding from states enacting 'onerous' AI laws. The order signaled carve-outs for child safety and AI compute/data-center infrastructure.
committees_and_bodies.status: VERIFIED — as of 1 July 2026 states had still enacted 109 AI laws and 28 data-center laws in 2026, versus 121 and 27 at the same point in 2025. Roughly 61% of Republican-controlled and 69% of Democratic-controlled states enacted AI legislation, so the chilling effect was real but not partisan. Concrete litigation consequences: x.AI's challenge restrained Colorado AG enforcement; xAI sued Minnesota over its nudification ban and lost its bid to pause it.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: N/A at the federal level for these actions, but this is precisely why state-level testimony matters more right now: Virginia legislators explicitly cited the federal order when tabling AI bills to 2027, and child-safety framing is the carve-out that is still moving. Framing state testimony around child safety and around data-center/ratepayer impacts is currently the path of least resistance.
committees_and_bodies.agency_route: N/A
committees_and_bodies.note: Context entry. The practical implication for a member of the public: the 2027 sessions (Virginia, Texas, and the carry-over dockets in Virginia and New Jersey) are where the deferred AI bills return, and the testimony windows open January–March 2027.

committees_and_bodies.body: House of Commons Science and Technology Committee (committee id 135; formerly the Science, Innovation and Technology Committee)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Commons departmental select committee for science, research and technology policy. Following the abolition of DSIT in July 2026 its title reverted to 'Science and Technology Committee'. It scrutinises AI research, compute, AI in government, and has written to Government on UK AI sovereignty (letter reported 15 September 2026). Its live inquiries touch AI obliquely rather than head-on: 'Low-energy computing' (opened 16 April 2026) and 'Neuroscience and digital childhoods' (opened 24 March 2026).

chair.name: Dame Chi Onwurah MP (Labour, Newcastle upon Tyne Central and West)
chair.role: Chair

committees_and_bodies.key_people: George Freeman MP (Con) and Rt Hon Kit Malthouse MP (Con) are the senior opposition members; Dr Allison Gardner MP (Lab) sits on the committee AND chairs the APPG on AI — she is the single most efficient point of contact for AI in the Commons. Other members: Tom Collins, Emily Darlington, Maya Ellis, Samantha Niblett, Freddie van Mierlo (LD), Martin Wrigley (LD), Daniel Zeichner.
committees_and_bodies.business: 7 open inquiries as at 22 Sep 2026: Low-energy computing; Neuroscience and digital childhoods; Science and regulation of hair and beauty products; Innovation and global food security; Science diplomacy (reported 7 Jul 2026); Digital centre of government (reported 3 Jun 2026); Innovation showcase.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Submit written evidence to an open inquiry via the secure online portal linked from that inquiry's page. Anyone may submit — no need to be an expert or an organisation.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: Usually no more than 3,000 words; numbered paragraphs and headings; single Word/ODT/RTF file, max 25MB; no logos or decorative graphics. Must not have been published elsewhere. Accepted evidence becomes the property of the committee, is published online permanently and forms part of the parliamentary record; you may not republish it yourself until the committee authorises publication.
committees_and_bodies.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-22 from the committee's own membership and news pages. NAME CHANGE: the URL slug still reads 'science-innovation-and-technology-committee' but the page heading and browser title now read 'Science and Technology Committee'. No inquiry with 'AI' in the title is currently open here.

committees_and_bodies.body: House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee (committee id 365; formerly the Business and Trade Committee)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Departmental select committee for the new Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST), which absorbed much of the abolished DSIT. It ran the inquiry 'Artificial Intelligence, business and the future of the workforce' — the most substantial Commons AI inquiry of this Parliament. AI's effect on employment, skills, business adoption and industrial strategy sits here.

chair.name: Rt Hon Liam Byrne MP (Labour, Birmingham Hodge Hill and Solihull North)
chair.role: Chair

committees_and_bodies.key_people: Members: Dan Aldridge, Antonia Bance, Chris Bloore, John Cooper (Con), Sarah Edwards, Alison Griffiths (Con), Leigh Ingham, Justin Madders, Charlie Maynard (LD), Joshua Reynolds (LD).
committees_and_bodies.business: 'Artificial Intelligence, business and the future of the workforce' (work id 9674) — written evidence CLOSED at 11:59pm on 3 April 2026; the committee is in the report/oral-evidence phase.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Written evidence when a call is open; otherwise write to the Chair or the committee clerk, and watch for the next call for evidence.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: Standard Commons rules: usually max 3,000 words, numbered paragraphs, single editable file under 25MB, published permanently.
committees_and_bodies.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-22. The committee page URL still says 'business-and-trade-committee' but the membership page heading reads 'Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee' — renamed after the July 2026 machinery-of-government changes. The AI/workforce inquiry is no longer accepting evidence.

committees_and_bodies.body: House of Lords Communications and Digital Committee
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: The Lords' standing committee on media, broadcasting, telecoms and the digital economy. It is the UK's most productive parliamentary venue on AI policy: it produced 'AI, copyright and the creative industries' (4th Report, published 6 March 2026; Government response 15 May 2026) and is now examining the Online Safety Act, where AI-generated content and algorithmic systems are squarely in scope.

chair.name: The Baroness Keeley (Labour life peer)
chair.role: Chair

committees_and_bodies.key_people: Viscount Colville of Culross (Crossbench), Lord Holmes of Richmond MBE (Con) — a persistent AI-regulation campaigner in the Lords, Lord Knight of Weymouth (Lab), Lord Tarassenko CBE FREng (Crossbench) — an AI/engineering academic, Baroness Owen of Alderley Edge (Con) — deepfake legislation, Baroness Fleet, Baroness Caine of Kentish Town, Baroness Elliott of Whitburn Bay, Lord Kirkhope of Harrogate, Lord McNally (LD), Lord Storey (LD), Lord Bishop of Winchester. 13 members total.
committees_and_bodies.business: 2 current inquiries: 'The Online Safety Act: implementation and impact' (opened 27 July 2026, written evidence deadline 21 September 2026 — now closed); 'AI and copyright' (opened 3 Nov 2025, reported 6 March 2026, Government response 15 May 2026).
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Written evidence via the portal on the inquiry page. Lords committees receive far fewer submissions than Commons ones, so a competent submission has a much higher chance of being cited.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: Same Parliament-wide rules: usually max 3,000 words, numbered paragraphs, single Word/ODT/RTF file under 25MB, not previously published, published online permanently, covered by parliamentary privilege once accepted.
committees_and_bodies.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-22 from the committee's membership page. Baroness Keeley is listed as 'Chair Lords'. The Online Safety Act evidence window closed the day before this check (21 Sep 2026).

committees_and_bodies.body: UK Parliament — select committee written evidence system (the key public route)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Not a body but the mechanism: every Commons, Lords and Joint select committee inquiry runs on written evidence solicited from the public. This is the only route by which an ordinary member of the public can put a document directly into the parliamentary record and have MPs' staff read it.

chair.role: Not applicable — administered by each committee's clerk

committees_and_bodies.key_people: The committee clerk (not the Chair) is the decision-maker on whether a submission is accepted and published. Contact details for each clerk are on the committee's page.
committees_and_bodies.business: Inquiries VERIFIED as accepting written evidence on 22 Sep 2026 include: 'The Online Safety Act: implementation and impact' (Lords Communications and Digital, deadline 21 Sep 2026); 'Regulatory sandboxes in financial services' (deadline 23 Oct 2026); 'Climate adaptation' (deadline 21 Oct 2026); 'Dunkelflaute and the risks of electricity intermittency' (deadline 12 Oct 2026); 'Clean Power by 2030: Upgrading the grid' (deadline 8 Oct 2026). No inquiry titled on AI is open as at this date.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Browse all open calls at the filtered inquiries URL, open the inquiry page, click the call for evidence, and upload through the secure portal. No invitation, credential or sponsorship is needed; individuals may submit on the same footing as corporations.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: EXACT RULES from the official guidance: 'Committees value clear and concise submissions, usually no more than 3,000 words.' Structure with numbered paragraphs and headings; plain English with technical terms explained; a single Word, ODT or RTF file (NOT PDF), maximum 25MB; no logos, decorative graphics or repeated headers/footers. If longer than 3,000 words, put a summary at the start. Your evidence must not have been published elsewhere, though you may cite published material. Deadline convention: each call states a date, normally 6–10 weeks after opening, and cut-off is 11:59pm on that day; late submissions are often still accepted at the clerk's discretion if the report is not yet drafted — ask the clerk. Once accepted, evidence becomes the property of the committee, is published online and 'stays public forever' as part of the permanent parliamentary record; you cannot republish it yourself until the committee authorises it. You may request anonymity or confidentiality but the committee decides.
committees_and_bodies.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-22 against https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm/written-evidence-guidance.htm (the official House of Commons written evidence guidance) and the live open-inquiries filter.

committees_and_bodies.body: All-Party Parliamentary Group on Artificial Intelligence (APPG AI)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Cross-party, cross-House informal group. Its registered purpose: 'The APPG explores the social, economic and societal impact and implications of artificial intelligence.' It has no formal powers but it convenes ministers, officials and MPs, runs evidence sessions and publishes reports — and unlike a select committee it is genuinely open to unsolicited outside contact.

committees_and_bodies.body: European Parliament — Committee on the Internal Market and Consumer Protection (IMCO)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Co-lead committee on the AI Act and its successors. IMCO owns the AI Act as a product-safety and internal-market instrument: placing AI systems on the market, conformity assessment, high-risk classification, obligations on providers and deployers, and consumer protection. It was joint-lead with LIBE on the Digital Omnibus on AI and is lead on the Cloud and AI Development Act.

The seats that actually matter on AI are not the Vice-Chairs but the file-holders: Brando Benifei (S&D, IT) — AI Act co-rapporteur in the previous term and IMCO co-chair of the AI Act Working Group; Arba Kokalari (EPP, SE) — IMCO rapporteur on the Digital Omnibus on AI; Reinier van Lanschot (Greens/EFA, NL) — IMCO rapporteur on the Cloud and AI Development Act; Alex Agius Saliba (S&D, MT).

committees_and_bodies.public_route: Three real routes: (1) email the rapporteur and every shadow rapporteur on the file directly — MEP addresses are public and they read constituent-independent mail; (2) file a petition through PETI, which is the only formal citizen channel into Parliament; (3) attend or watch committee meetings, which are webstreamed, and submit through a registered organisation's position paper. Anyone paid to influence should be on the EU Transparency Register; MEPs are required to publish meetings with registered interest representatives. Nothing sent to an MEP is automatically published.

committees_and_bodies.body: European Parliament — Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Co-lead committee on the AI Act. LIBE owns the fundamental-rights half: prohibited practices (Article 5), biometric identification, emotion recognition, predictive policing, AI in migration and law enforcement, and the interaction with GDPR. Joint-lead with IMCO on the Digital Omnibus on AI and co-owner of the AI Act Working Group.

committees_and_bodies.body: European Parliament — IMCO-LIBE Joint Working Group on the Implementation and Enforcement of the Artificial Intelligence Act
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: EXACT REMIT, quoted from the Parliament's own page: 'By a decision of IMCO and LIBE Coordinators, a joint Working Group on the implementation and enforcement of the Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) was established with the purpose of monitoring and scrutinizing the implementation and enforcement of the AI Act.' In practice it is Parliament's standing oversight body over the Commission's AI Office: it presses on AI Office staffing and transparency, the role of civil society in implementation, delegated and implementing acts, guidelines, standards, national competent authorities, regulatory sandboxes and real-world testing.

Between them these two MEPs are the most important individual AI seats in the entire European Parliament. The Working Group's member list is published as a downloadable document on its page.

Reach it by writing to either co-chair — Benifei and McNamara both publish office emails on their MEP pages — with a short, specific, evidenced point about AI Act implementation. Because the Working Group's job is to find enforcement gaps, credible evidence of a gap is exactly what it wants and there is almost no competition for its attention.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: No formal rules. Keep to 1–2 pages naming the specific AI Act article, the specific failure, and the specific ask. Not published.

committees_and_bodies.body: European Parliament — the rapporteur and shadow rapporteur system (the highest-leverage seats in EU legislating)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: Applies to every AI legislative file. WHAT A RAPPORTEUR IS: when the Commission sends a legislative proposal to Parliament, one committee is designated lead. Within that committee the political groups bid for the file using an auction system based on group size, and the winning group appoints ONE MEP as rapporteur. That single MEP drafts Parliament's report — the consolidated set of amendments that becomes Parliament's official position — decides which of the thousands of tabled amendments are folded into compromise texts, chairs the technical meetings, and then personally leads Parliament's delegation in the closed trilogue negotiations with the Council and Commission where the final law is actually written. WHAT A SHADOW RAPPORTEUR IS: every other political group appoints one shadow to follow the same file. Shadows negotiate the compromise amendments with the rapporteur; a compromise that the EPP, S&D and Renew shadows sign will pass, and one they refuse will not. The rapporteur plus roughly six shadows — under ten people — effectively write EU law on a given file. This is why the rapporteur seat is worth more than a committee chair: the chair runs the meeting, the rapporteur writes the text.

chair.name: Michael McNamara (Renew Europe, Ireland)
chair.role: Rapporteur, Digital Omnibus on AI (2025/0359(COD)); LIBE co-chair of the AI Act Working Group

committees_and_bodies.key_people: CURRENT AI FILE-HOLDERS, verified 2026-09-22: Digital Omnibus on AI, 2025/0359(COD), joint IMCO-LIBE — rapporteurs Arba Kokalari (EPP, Sweden) and Michael McNamara (Renew, Ireland). Cloud and AI Development Act, 2026/0138(COD) — IMCO rapporteur Reinier van Lanschot (Greens/EFA, Netherlands), appointed September 2026. AI Act implementation oversight — Brando Benifei (S&D, Italy) and Michael McNamara. Shadow rapporteurs are listed on each file's page in the Legislative Observatory (oeil.europarl.europa.eu) under 'Committee opinion / Shadow rapporteur' — I did not verify the individual shadows by name and am not asserting them.
committees_and_bodies.business: Cloud and AI Development Act 2026/0138(COD) is the live AI file: Commission proposal 3 June 2026, rapporteur appointed September 2026, committee stage running now — which means the amendment window is OPEN and this is the moment at which outside input has effect. The Digital Omnibus on AI is closed: provisional trilogue agreement 7 May 2026, Coreper 13 May 2026, IMCO/LIBE approval 2 June 2026, plenary adoption 16 June 2026 (423 for, 57 against, 174 abstentions).
committees_and_bodies.public_route: HOW AN OUTSIDER ACTUALLY REACHES A RAPPORTEUR: (1) Identify the file and its holders in the Legislative Observatory (oeil.europarl.europa.eu) or the Legislative Train (europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train) — both list the procedure number, lead committee and rapporteur. (2) Go to that MEP's page at europarl.europa.eu/meps/en/<id> which publishes their Brussels and Strasbourg office email and phone. (3) Write to the rapporteur AND every shadow at once — reaching only the rapporteur means your point dies if their group disagrees with it. (4) Time it to the draft-report and amendment-tabling window, which is the only period at which text can still change; after a trilogue deal nothing moves. (5) Say what you want in amendment form: name the article, give replacement wording, give one paragraph of justification. Rapporteurs' assistants triage hundreds of submissions and the ones that arrive as usable text get used. (6) An MEP office will normally meet a credible outside party; ask for a 20-minute meeting with the policy adviser, not the MEP. If you are paid to do this you must register on the EU Transparency Register first.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: No word limit, no portal, no deadline other than the committee's amendment-tabling deadline (published on the file page). Correspondence is not published. If you are an interest representative, entry in the EU Transparency Register is a precondition of meeting MEPs holding rapporteur roles, and such meetings must be declared.
committees_and_bodies.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-22: rapporteur identities from the European Parliament Legislative Train Schedule file pages for the Digital Omnibus on AI and the Cloud and AI Development Act. The procedural description of the rapporteur/shadow system is standard EP practice under the Rules of Procedure, not a claim about a named individual. Individual shadow rapporteurs are deliberately NOT named here because I did not verify them.

committees_and_bodies.body: European Parliament — Committee on Petitions (PETI)
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: PETI has no AI portfolio of its own, but it is the ONLY formal channel through which a private individual can compel the European Parliament to consider a matter. An admissible AI petition — for example on AI Act non-enforcement in a Member State, biometric surveillance, or algorithmic discrimination — is put to the committee, can trigger questions to the Commission, a committee debate, a fact-finding visit, or a referral to LIBE or IMCO.

chair.name: Bogdan Rzońca (ECR, Poland, Prawo i Sprawiedliwość)
chair.role: Chair

committees_and_bodies.key_people: Vice-Chairs: Dolors Montserrat (EPP, ES); Fredis Beleris (EPP, GR); Nils Ušakovs (S&D, LV); Cristina Guarda (Greens/EFA, IT). The committee has 35 members.
committees_and_bodies.business: Ordinary petition sittings roughly monthly; agendas published as PETI_OJ documents on europarl.europa.eu/doceo.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: WHO MAY PETITION: 'Any citizen of the European Union, or resident in a Member State', individually or collectively, and 'any company, organisation or association with its headquarters in the European Union'. SUBJECT MATTER: the petition must concern a matter 'which comes within the European Union's fields of activity and which affects them directly' — this is the admissibility test and the most common reason petitions are rejected. It may be a complaint, a request, or an observation on the application of EU law, or an appeal for Parliament to take a position. PROCESS: file through the Petitions Web Portal in any of the 24 official EU languages; the secretariat assesses admissibility; admissible petitions go to the committee, which may ask the Commission for a preliminary investigation, put the petition on a meeting agenda, invite the petitioner to speak, refer it to another committee for opinion, or close it with a reasoned reply. THRESHOLD: there is NO signature threshold — one person suffices. (Do not confuse this with the European Citizens' Initiative, which does require one million signatures across at least seven Member States; that is a separate instrument aimed at the Commission, not Parliament.)
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: No word limit. Available in all 24 official EU languages. Petitions and the committee's handling of them are published on the petitions portal unless the petitioner requests confidentiality. You may support an existing petition rather than filing a new one.
committees_and_bodies.note: VERIFIED 2026-09-22: chair from the official PETI member list PDF; eligibility and subject-matter wording quoted from the European Parliament's own 'Be heard — petitions' page at europarl.europa.eu/at-your-service/en/be-heard/petitions.

committees_and_bodies.body: European Commission — Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy
committees_and_bodies.ai_jurisdiction: The Commissioner-level holder of the digital and AI portfolio: owns the AI Act's implementation through DG CNECT and the AI Office, the Digital Omnibus simplification agenda, the Cloud and AI Development Act, the Apply AI strategy, and AI gigafactory/compute policy. The Commission has the exclusive right of legislative initiative, so this is where AI files begin.

chair.name: Henna Virkkunen
chair.role: Executive Vice-President of the European Commission for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy

committees_and_bodies.key_people: Operational work sits with DG CNECT and the European AI Office within it.
committees_and_bodies.business: AI Act implementation following the Digital Omnibus on AI (adopted 16 June 2026, delaying high-risk system standards and banning 'nudifier' applications); Cloud and AI Development Act proposed 3 June 2026.
committees_and_bodies.public_route: Respond to open consultations on the 'Have your say' portal; write to the Cabinet; or use the AI Act Service Desk for regulatory questions. Commission consultations are open to anyone worldwide, not only EU residents.
committees_and_bodies.format_rules: Consultation responses are normally published on the initiative's feedback page together with the respondent's name and country, and organisations must give their EU Transparency Register number. You can ask for anonymity. Feedback periods for a 'call for evidence' are typically 4 weeks; full public consultations run 12 weeks.
